Where it began

Shane Bond was born in Christchurch on 7 June 1975 and went to Papanui High School. He came to first-class cricket late for a fast bowler, making his debut for Canterbury against Central Districts in January 1997, at 21, and he played only a dozen games in his first three seasons.

Then things moved quickly. A strong showing for the New Zealand academy against Australia's young players earned him a place on the 2001–02 tour of Australia, and he was picked for the Hobart Test ahead of Chris Martin because he was the quicker of the two.

The player

The Tests on that tour were hard going, but the one-day series that followed was another story: 21 wickets in nine games and the player-of-the-tournament award. He kept saving his best for Australia. He took 5 for 25 to beat them in January 2002, and 6 for 23 against them at the 2003 World Cup, then New Zealand's best one-day bowling. In 2007 his 5 for 23 helped New Zealand to their first clean sweep in the Chappell–Hadlee Trophy.

In Tests he was the leading wicket-taker when New Zealand won a series in the West Indies for the first time, in 2002, and he signed off with a match-winning return against Pakistan at Dunedin in 2009. Injury cut his Test career short, but his 18 matches brought 87 wickets at 22.09, with five five-wicket hauls and a best of 6 for 51.

What made him special

He was very fast, often above 145 km/h, and once timed at 156.4 km/h against India at the 2003 World Cup. Plenty of bowlers are quick. What set Bond apart was that he could be quick and accurate at the same time, which is why he took wickets so often. In January 2007 he reached 100 one-day international wickets in only his 54th match. New Zealand made him their cricketer of the year in 2007.

With the bat he was usually found at nine or lower. He could, though, swing for a couple of late boundaries, and once made an unbeaten 41 in a Test, which must have surprised a few bowlers.

Away from the middle

He became a respected coach. As New Zealand's bowling coach from October 2012 he was credited with helping Trent Boult and Tim Southee, and he left after the 2015 World Cup, in which New Zealand reached the final. He went on to coach Mumbai Indians and Brisbane Heat, became head coach of Sydney Thunder in 2018, and joined the Sky Sports commentary team. He told his story in an autobiography written with Dylan Cleaver.

And finally

On his first County Championship appearance for Hampshire, in 2008, he took 7 for 66 against Sussex, the reigning champions. Some players take a while to settle into a new team. Bond did not seem to need long.
